topics.title: National Affairs: PM-JAY, Make in India, UDAN and Governance Updates
facts: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY completed eight years on 23 September 2026. More than 60 crore beneficiaries have been covered; the scheme was launched at Ranchi on 23 September 2018. Arogya Manthan 2026 launched the National Healthcare Providers Registry Mobile App, Secure Data Environment and Auto-Adjudication Framework, while ABDM completed five years.

Make in India completed 12 years on 25 September. Launched in 2014, it now covers manufacturing, electronics, automobiles, pharmaceuticals, defence, steel, solar manufacturing and startups, with policy emphasis moving from assembly to domestic value chains, design and innovation.
The National Single Window System provides investors with a single digital interface for approvals and clearances across departments and governments, reducing the need to approach multiple agencies.

The next phase of UDAN was launched with MoUs involving 22 States and UTs. A Challenge Mode Portal for aerodrome development allows nominations of airstrips and helipads, after which airlines bid for routes.

The President amended the Inter-State Council Order, 1990 under Article 263. During Article 356 President’s Rule, a State Governor may be invited to Inter-State Council meetings; for Delhi, the Lieutenant Governor may be invited when Article 239AB applies.
DILRMP integrates land records, cadastral maps, registration and GIS through unique land identification; the 14-digit ULPIN or Bhu-Aadhaar remains important for Prelims.

The National Steering Committee approved a ₹320 crore Strategic Investment Plan for the Kurukshetra ITI Cluster under PM-SETU. It integrates seven government ITIs, with Jindal Naveen Avsar Limited as anchor partner; cumulative PM-SETU investment reached about ₹2,491 crore across 10 clusters.

The 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan was launched through MY Bharat and NSS. The Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh began on 18 September, mobilising over four lakh participants across more than 1,000 locations under Prevent, Protect, Recover and Lead.

Swachh Seva Aankalan was launched as an annual digital self-assessment framework for rural sanitation under SBM-Grameen 2.0. Gram Panchayats assess ODF sustainability, visual cleanliness, waste management and sanitation assets, with Gram Sabha validation.
A Joint Parliamentary Committee began examining the Foreign Contribution Regulation Amendment Bill, 2026, covering NGO regulation, internal security, transparency and civil-society financing.
The 72nd National Film Awards were presented during the week; veteran Kannada actor Anant Nag received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, India’s highest cinema honour.
topics.detail: The week covered health and digital-health milestones, manufacturing policy, investor clearances, regional aviation, federal institutions, land records, skilling, de-addiction, sanitation, FCRA oversight and cinema honours.
topics.exam: Remember PM-JAY dates and coverage, Make in India, Articles 263, 356 and 239AB, UDAN’s 22 MoUs, Kurukshetra PM-SETU, the four Nasha Mukt pillars and Swachh Seva Aankalan.

topics.title: International Affairs: New Zealand FTA, ASEAN, Bhutan and Military Exercises
facts: India and New Zealand completed domestic processes for their Free Trade Agreement, which enters into force on 20 October 2026. All Indian exports to New Zealand receive duty-free access from day one, with benefits for textiles, apparel, leather, footwear, engineering, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and processed food; the agreement facilitates about US$20 billion investment into India and expands mobility.

India participated in the 23rd ASEAN–India Economic Ministers’ Consultation and 14th East Asia Summit Economic Ministers’ Meeting in Manila. AITIGA review was important; India–ASEAN trade reached about US$128.38 billion in 2025–26, around 10.55% of India’s total global trade.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar’s Bhutan visit and continuing developments covered hydropower, connectivity, healthcare, education, fintech and clean mobility. India extended a concessional ₹4,000 crore Line of Credit for Bhutan’s energy sector.
The 13th SLINEX-26 India–Sri Lanka naval exercise was conducted at Visakhapatnam to strengthen maritime cooperation, interoperability, mutual understanding and joint operational capability.
The 24th edition of Exercise VARUNA between the Indian and French Navies was conducted at Toulon, France, with harbour and sea phases, operational interactions and cross-deck activities.

The 18th India–Mongolia joint military exercise Nomadic Elephant 2026 began at Pithoragarh from 21 September to 3 October, focusing on cordon and search, room intervention, special heliborne operations, cybersecurity, drones and counter-drone systems.
topics.detail: International coverage focused on trade liberalisation, ASEAN economic integration, Bhutan energy cooperation and three maritime or land military exercises.
topics.exam: Remember the FTA effective date and duty-free coverage, AITIGA and trade figures, Bhutan’s credit line, and the partners, editions and venues of SLINEX, VARUNA and Nomadic Elephant.
topics.remember: India–NZ FTA: 20 October 2026; duty-free exports: 100%; SLINEX: India–Sri Lanka; VARUNA: India–France; Nomadic Elephant: India–Mongolia.

topics.title: Economy, Banking and Business: Exports, Inflation, REITs and Social Security
facts: The India–New Zealand FTA will provide duty-free access for Indian exports from 20 October 2026, facilitate about US$20 billion investment and improve market access for selected New Zealand products such as wood, wool and agriculture.

RBI’s annual survey placed India’s software-services exports at about US$221.4 billion in FY2025–26, up 8.2% year on year. The US held a 54.1% share with about US$119.7 billion, while Europe accounted for about 31.8%.

India’s August 2026 WPI inflation was 9.92%, up from 9.78% in July. August rates were 7.76% for Primary Articles, 22.93% for Fuel and Power and 8.37% for Manufactured Products; fuel and power were the strongest pressure source.
Moody’s raised India’s FY2026–27 GDP growth forecast to 7% from 6%, retained the Baa3 sovereign rating with stable outlook and cited resilience while flagging energy-price and El Niño risks.
India’s REIT market reached about US$17.7 billion, overtaking Hong Kong as Asia’s fourth-largest REIT market. RBI also revised valuation norms for REIT and InvIT units held by financial institutions.

NSE enabled India’s first tokenised corporate-bond issuances worth ₹1,000 crore under the SEBI Regulatory Sandbox Framework: REC and Larsen & Toubro raised ₹500 crore each using blockchain/tokenisation.
GFCI 40 ranked GIFT City 37th globally, while New York topped the financial-centre rankings; GIFT City continues to develop as India’s international financial-services hub.
The government approved raising the EPFO wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month to expand formal social-security coverage.
GOBARdhan guidelines included assured offtake arrangements for compressed biogas, supporting waste-to-energy and circular-economy objectives.
India–ASEAN trade was approximately US$128.38 billion in FY2025–26; AITIGA review remains relevant to trade barriers and asymmetries.

topics.title: Science and Technology: Quantum Cryogenics, NETRA, AI and New Materials
facts: DRDO signed its first high-value deep-tech Technology Development Fund agreement with Zero mK India to develop an indigenous 20 millikelvin dilution refrigerator, approximately 0.02 Kelvin, for quantum-computing hardware and reduced dependence on imported infrastructure.

ISRO and ESA extended their cooperation agreement until 8 January 2032, expanding work in human and robotic exploration, space weather, sustainable outer-space activities, Earth observation, space science and navigation.

Assam laid the foundation for ISRO’s ISTRAC Advanced Radar Research Facility at Chandrapur, Kamrup Metropolitan, under NETRA. The facility will improve Space Situational Awareness; Assam provided about 70 acres and the first radar is expected around February 2027.
The Technology Development Board agreed to provide GalaxEye about ₹63.84 crore for next-generation multisensor satellite technology for Earth observation and remote sensing.
The Technology Development Board provided about ₹285 crore RDI support to Ubifly Technologies for next-generation air-mobility technologies and indigenous advanced aviation systems.

Raman Research Institute researchers measured a quantum measure of about 1.17, close to a predicted 1.18. It relates to Quantum Measure Theory and does not mean photon-detection probability exceeds one; the effect arises from quantum interference.
IIEST Shibpur and TCS signed an MoU for an AI Centre of Excellence focused on NLP, computer vision, image processing, data analytics, AI research and startup innovation.

The government highlighted commercial bio-based biodegradable plastic under the BioE3 initiative to reduce dependence on petroleum-based plastics; food-safety regulation, testing, traceability and consumer protection also remained important themes.
topics.detail: Science and technology developments linked quantum hardware, space cooperation and radar-based SSA with multisensor satellites, air mobility, AI and sustainable materials.
topics.exam: Remember 20 mK, the ISRO–ESA end date, NETRA location and land, both TDB amounts, quantum measure 1.17, AI CoE partners and BioE3.
topics.remember: Quantum refrigerator: 20 mK; NETRA radar: Chandrapur, Assam; GalaxEye: ₹63.84 crore; Ubifly: ₹285 crore.

topics.title: Environment and Ecology: Circular Economy, Soil Carbon and Great Nicobar Minerals
facts: World Circular Economy Forum 2026 was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, making India the first South Asian host. Its theme was “Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity”, with resource efficiency, waste reduction, recycling, reuse and Extended Producer Responsibility as focus areas.

India initiated its first farm-level soil-carbon payments in Punjab. About 2,550 smallholder farmers from Punjab and Haryana were to receive more than ₹2.9 crore for Direct Seeded Rice, reduced tillage and crop-residue management linked to verified carbon credits.

Begonia neelamorum, a new flowering plant, was discovered in Keyi Panyor district, Arunachal Pradesh, around 1,000 metres elevation. It was provisionally classified Data Deficient under IUCN criteria and named after the Neelam clan of the Nyishi community.
Researchers documented 3,261 flowering plant species in the Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, reinforcing the Western Ghats’ status as a biodiversity hotspot.

The Ministry of Mines notified two offshore mineral blocks near Great Nicobar: West Sewell Ridge-01 of 1,000 sq km and Sewell Rise-01 of 632 sq km, together 1,632 sq km. Target minerals include polymetallic nodules and crusts containing nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper and rare-earth elements, raising blue-economy, biodiversity, tribal-rights and marine-conservation questions.
BRIC-NIPGR’s SPROUT facility was highlighted for climate-resilient crop research and varieties better suited to climate stresses.
topics.detail: Environmental coverage connected circular economy, verified farm carbon credits, biodiversity discoveries, Western Ghats conservation, deep-ocean minerals and climate-resilient crops.
topics.exam: Remember WCEF host and theme, soil-carbon amount and practices, Begonia location and status, Agasthyamalai count, Great Nicobar block areas and minerals.

topics.title: Defence and Security: Exercises, APUs, Smart Weapons and SSA
facts: Nomadic Elephant 2026 is the 18th India–Mongolia Army exercise at Pithoragarh, focusing on counter-insurgency, cordon and search, heliborne operations, cybersecurity, drones and counter-drones.
SLINEX-26 is the 13th India–Sri Lanka naval exercise at Visakhapatnam, focused on maritime interoperability and joint operational capability.
VARUNA 2026 is the 24th India–France naval exercise at Toulon, with harbour and sea phases.

The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹586 crore contract for 3,257 Auxiliary Power Units: 1,657 for T-90 tanks and 1,600 for T-72 tanks. APUs operate critical systems without running the main engine and support Make-II indigenisation.

The Ministry of Defence signed an ₹811 crore contract with Bharat Dynamics Limited for 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons for the Indian Air Force, supporting indigenous precision-strike capability.
DRDO’s first high-value deep-tech TDF project, the 20 mK dilution refrigerator, links defence R&D with India’s quantum ecosystem.
A National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports team summited 20 previously unclimbed peaks above 6,000 metres in Ladakh in 23 days, covering Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala and Chokula.
The Indian Coast Guard participated in the QUAD-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission to support maritime cooperation among QUAD countries.

topics.title: Sports: Asian Games Cricket, Kabaddi and Subroto Cup
facts: The 20th Asian Games are being held in Aichi–Nagoya, Japan, from 19 September to 4 October 2026.

India defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the Women’s T20 final, scoring 216/3 against Sri Lanka’s 69. Smriti Mandhana scored 79 and Shafali Verma 48; India won its first 2026 Asian Games gold through women’s T20 cricket.
Smriti Mandhana became the first woman to reach 11,000 international runs during the Asian Games Women’s T20 final.
India won both men’s and women’s kabaddi gold medals. The women defeated Iran 37–34 and the men defeated Iran 40–34, retaining both Asian Games titles.

By the end of 26 September, India had 4 gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze medals, 30 in total, and stood 10th in the medal table. Other performances included Kamaljeet and Suruchi Inder Singh’s 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team gold, Gulveer Singh and Tajinderpal Singh Toor silver medals, a Mixed 4×400m Relay silver, and bronze medals for Manpreet Kaur, Baranica Elangovan, Joshna Chinappa–Velavan Senthilkumar and Manush Shah–Diya Chitale.

The 65th Subroto Cup concluded: Minerva Public School, Mohali won Junior Boys U-17 by defeating MIC EMHSS Kerala 3–2; St Patrick’s High School, Gumla won Junior Girls and Manik Para Vivekanand Vidyapeeth, Jhargram won Sub-Junior Boys.
